newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Democrats say budget not too bad.
newsitem.headline: Australian Democrats say budget not too bad.

text.p: The Australian Democrats Party, which could control the balance of power in the Senate needed to pass budget bills, said on Tuesday there was not too much that it would object to in the government's budget for 1997/98.
"There's not much that's going to find a hostile reception within this budget," Australian Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot told reporters in Canberra.
Kernot said however that the Democrats were not happy with the government's plan to offer a 15 percent tax rebate for interest income from savings up to A$3,000 per year.
She said 43 percent of Australians earning less than A$35,000 had no savings and the plan favoured high income earners who could afford to save.
"It's very badly designed and skewed towards high income earners," he said.
"We'll probably need to look at modifying that," she said.
